entry.evidence: the aim of this study is to compare the temperatures calculated from the measured noble gas concentrations to actual mean annual air and soil temperatures

steps.action: Cite the standing assumption, resting on Stute and Schlosser's ground-temperature profile modelling, that MAST equals MAAT, so NGT records MAAT at recharge.
steps.quote: derived from the assumption that the mean annual soil temperature (MAST) should be equal to the MAAT

steps.action: Cite the rival position (Beyerle et al., Smith et al., Stute and Sonntag, Klump et al.) that NGT reflects soil temperature and exceeds MAAT, depending on vegetation, climate and unsaturated-zone thickness.
steps.quote: NGTs of young samples (<1 kyr BP) rather reflect soil temperature and both are higher than MAAT

steps.action: Choose the closed-system equilibration (CE) excess-air model and set aside the oxygen-depletion and PR models, citing near-atmospheric dissolved oxygen (2-8 mg/L) and Freundt et al. (2013).
steps.quote: we assumed that oxygen depletion does not play a significant role, thus only the CE-model was applied

steps.action: Pose the aim: compare NGTs with actual mean annual air and soil temperatures [...] sampling sites.
steps.quote: the aim of this study is to compare the temperatures calculated from the measured noble gas concentrations

steps.action: Select six Hungarian micro-regions (three sandy alluvial plains, a loess hill region, two karst mountains) that span hydrogeological and meso-climatic conditions, described with the Feddema classification.
steps.quote: in order to study the influence of these factors on the relation of NGT and mean annual temperature values

steps.action: Sample springs and shallow wells in copper tubes and measure Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe and He isotopes by noble gas mass spectrometry, part of the data having been published earlier.
steps.quote: Water samples for noble gas analysis were collected in copper tubes clamped at both ends and analyzed for Ne, Ar, Kr and Xe isotopes

steps.action: Check the premises of the NGT model: 3H/3He ages confirm young water, He is excluded for its terrigenic component, and 20Ne/22Ne ratios confirm solubility equilibrium.
steps.quote: In most cases, the solubility of equilibrium has been achieved confirmed by 20Ne/22Ne ratios of 9.78 ± 0.02.

steps.action: Infer recharge temperatures (NGT) by inverse modelling of Ne, Ar, Kr and Xe concentrations with the CE model.
steps.quote: Estimated recharge temperatures of the investigated wells and springs were calculated with the Noble90 and the Noblebook.

steps.action: Run the inversion in two codes (Noble90 and Noblebook) and report that they give the same values.
steps.quote: [...] the same values but Noble90 gives the uncertainties of the NGTs.

steps.action: Obtain monthly air and soil temperatures for 2016 from ECMWF ERA-Interim at 0.125° resolution for each site.
steps.quote: Meteorological data (Table SM2) evaluated over a one-year interval (2016)

steps.action: Describe the monthly air and soil temperature curves per region: a two-month lag of soil behind air, MAST above MAAT everywhere, and Bükk coldest.
steps.quote: in all sampled regions similar trends of about a two-month-lag between air and soil temperature values can be observed

steps.action: Summarize per-region NGT distributions in a boxplot, separating mountains from plains, with an all-region mean of 11.2 ± 2.3 °C.
steps.quote: The distinctness of the sampled mountainous regions and alluvial plains can be observed.

steps.action: Compare the Bükk NGT with the expected local multi-annual temperature and find it lower than expected (6.8 versus 8-9 °C).
steps.quote: the calculated mean value of 6.8 ± 0.6 °C was less than the average multi-annual temperature of the sampled part of the region

steps.action: Repeat sampling across seasons (Bükk summer versus winter) and across years (Mecsek 4 years, Mezőföld 3 years) to show the low karst NGT is not a sampling-date artifact.
steps.quote: Mean NGT value of summer sampling was 7.24 ± 0.5 °C, while that of winter sampling was 6.28 ± 0.1 °C.

steps.action: Compare the other regional NGTs with literature regional mean temperatures: Mecsek matches (10-11 °C), while Geresd and Nyírség lie 2-3 °C above.
steps.quote: The mean calculated noble gas temperature of Geresd Hills (13.0 ± 0.9 °C) was 2-3 °C higher than the known average mean annual temperature

steps.action: Compare their MAAT and MAST relation with Smith et al. (1964): soil temperature is slightly above air temperature in temperate climate.
steps.quote: The data resemble the early findings of Smith et al. (32) regarding the relationship of MAAT and MAST

steps.action: Compare the Mecsek NGT with ERA-Interim MAAT and MAST (Table 1) and judge it closer to MAAT.
steps.quote: it seems that calculated noble gas temperature (10.7 ± 1.9 °C) is closer to the values of MAAT (11.8 °C)

steps.action: Cite Stute and Schlosser's explanation that karst recharge lacks time to equilibrate with ground air, and qualify it for covered karst.
steps.quote: in karstic areas the recharging water does not have enough time for equilibration with the ground air which results in lower recharge temperature

steps.action: Compare the Bükk NGT with MAAT and MAST and find it far below both.
steps.quote: MAAT (10.7 °C) and MAST (11.1 °C) data were not very different, but the calculated NGT was even lower (6.8 ± 0.6 °C)

steps.action: Propose that thin soil cover and rapid infiltration through dolines and sinkholes limit heat and gas exchange in karst, and list rivals: preferential-flow surface temperature (Warrier et al.) and oxygen depletion (Hall et al.).
steps.quote: the infiltration can occur rapidly enough through dolines and sinkholes to make heat and also the gas exchange

steps.action: Set karst dissolved oxygen (3.2-6.4 mg/L) against the oxygen-depletion rival; the data do not support it, but it is not rejected.
steps.quote: well aerated conditions of karsts does not confirm this assumption, and we cannot reject it

steps.action: Compare Geresd Hills and the three sandy alluvial plains with MAAT and MAST and find their NGTs closer to MAST, attributed to recharge rate and geology.
steps.quote: show that the noble gas temperatures rather reflect the values of MAST instead of MAAT

steps.action: Keep the pattern: NGT reflects MAST on plains and hills and MAAT (or less) in karst, so NGT as a past-MAAT indicator can mislead.
steps.quote: it was confirmed that acceptance of NGT as an indicator of past mean air temperature can sometimes be misleading

steps.action: Keep the mechanism: differing air-water equilibration caused by rapid infiltration in karst aquifers.
steps.quote: differing equilibration mechanisms between air and water must be taking place in aquifers due to recharging from rapid infiltration processes

steps.action: Refine the use of noble gas paleothermometry: given local recharge conditions, decide whether NGT stands for MAAT or MAST.
steps.quote: noble gas paleothermometry can be a reliable tool for paleoclimate studies

end.claim: In the Hungarian sandy alluvial plains and loess hills NGT reflects mean annual soil temperature, while in the karst mountains it is close to or below mean annual air temperature, so MAAT and MAST must be distinguished when NGT is used as a paleotemperature proxy.

decisive_move.sentence: The region-by-region comparison of NGT with ERA-Interim MAAT and MAST in Table 1 is what separates the MAST-like plains and hills from the MAAT-like or lower karst sites.

gates.evidence: Regions were chosen to span hydrogeological and climatic conditions (§2.1 ¶1), but no stated hypothesis directed sampling, and part of the noble gas data was published earlier for recharge studies (§2.2 ¶1). The NGT-MAAT relation could have held everywhere, so the claim faced a test it could have failed. However, no statistical test is applied, and MAST-MAAT gaps are within NGT uncertainties for several regions (Table 1). Nothing is stated as fixed before the data.

imports.item: Henry's law temperature dependence of gas solubility
Noble gas mass spectrometry (VG 5400, Helix SFT)
Soil temperature regime relations (Smith et al. 1964, USDA)

limits: No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. (1) The meteorological comparison uses ERA-Interim reanalysis for one year (2016). NGT samples span up to four years and water ages up to 30 years (§2.1.2 ¶3, §2.1.3 ¶2). The paper cites Hall et al. (2012) recommending multi-year averaging (§1 ¶4) but does not address the mismatch. (2) No statistical test compares NGT with MAAT or MAST. MAST-MAAT gaps (0.4-1.3 °C) are comparable to or smaller than NGT 1σ errors. For example, Mecsek's 10.7 ± 1.9 °C cannot distinguish MAAT 11.8 from MAST 12.2 °C (inference from Table 1). (3) Bükk NGT is about 4 °C below both MAAT and MAST, so the conclusion that karst NGTs 'reflect mean annual air temperatures' overstates the match (inference). (4) Regional temperatures are inconsistent across the text: Bükk 6.5-7 and 8-9 °C in §2.1.5 versus ERA 10.7 °C; Nyírség 11-12 °C in §2.1.6 versus 9.7 °C in §3.2 versus 11.4 °C in Table 1. Fig. 2 labels the Danube-Tisza panel 'Bugac' (inference). (5) Part of the noble gas data was published earlier by overlapping authors (Szűcs et al. 2015; Palcsu et al. 2017); which samples is not stated. (6) Sample sizes are very unequal (Mecsek 55, Nyírség 7, Bükk 8). (7) Excess-air parameters are only in the supplement (Table SM3). (8) Sub-claims and statuses: the karst mechanism (rapid infiltration, insufficient equilibration) is best_explanation, with oxygen depletion explicitly not rejected; MAST > MAAT in all regions, consistent with Smith et al. 1964, is regularity_in_range.

disagreements.target: Common practice of using NGT to estimate MAAT (Hall et al. 2005; Castro et al. 2007; Mann et al. 2009), [...]
disagreements.support: In four of six regions NGT lies closer to MAST than MAAT, and in karst it lies near or below MAAT (Table 1).
disagreements.quote: the direct relationship between noble gas temperature and mean annual air temperature is not always as well-defined as it is often assumed

disagreements.target: Stute and Schlosser (1993): karst recharge lacks time to equilibrate, giving lower recharge temperatures
disagreements.support: Mecsek is covered karst, where soil slows infiltration and the NGT is not as depressed as at open-karst Bükk.
disagreements.quote: [...] Mts. is a covered karst where, comparing to an open karst, a soil layer can slow down infiltration processes.

disagreements.target: Oxygen depletion model of Hall et al. (2005)
disagreements.support: Dissolved oxygen of 2-8 mg/L (3.2-6.4 mg/L in karst) indicates near-atmospheric soil gas; Freundt et al. (2013) is cited for an overestimated effect; the model is not rejected.
disagreements.quote: well aerated conditions of karsts does not confirm this assumption, and we cannot reject it
